steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: You are working on Campfire, a Rails chat application. Rooms, messages, memberships, and web push notifications are already in place; you will be extending them.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

Follow the codebase conventions.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Bot authors asked for three things:

> As a bot author, I don't want my bot to end up in every open room. I want to
> choose the rooms it joins.

> As a bot author whose bot serves everyone, I don't want to add it to each
> open room by hand.

> As a bot author, I want to know when my bot lands in a new room, so it can
> say hello.

So bots no longer join open rooms by default. People still do.

The bot form (new and edit) gets a new switch:

- "Add to all open rooms" (off by default)

When the switch is on, the bot is a member of every open room: the ones that exist when the switch is turned on, and every open room that appears later. Turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships.

Whenever a bot is added to a room—automatically or by a person—its webhook receives a `joined` event, exactly once per room:

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/42-Xy3abc9defGh/messages" }
}
```

Direct conversations never trigger `joined`. The bot may reply to `joined` the same way as to `mention`: a `200` text or HTML reply is posted into that room as the bot's message.

# Campfire

Campfire is a web-based chat application. It supports many of the features you'd
expect, including:

- Multiple rooms, with access controls
- Direct messages
- File attachments with previews
- Search
- Notifications (via Web Push)
- Chat bots that post messages over HTTP, and that get a webhook when they're mentioned (see [bots](docs/bots.md))
- @mentions

## Running your own Campfire instance

Campfire's Docker image contains everything needed for a fully-functional,
single-machine deployment. This includes the web app, background jobs, caching,
file serving, and SSL. You can use our pre-built image at
`ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire:latest`, or build your own from this repo.

### Deploying with ONCE

The easiest way to self-host Campfire is with [ONCE](https://github.com/basecamp/once).
It will guide you through the initial set up and then keep your instance up to date automatically.

If you don't already have `once` installed, run this on the machine you want to run Campfire on:

```sh
curl https://get.once.com | sh
```

`once` will launch as soon as the install is finished. 

Choose Campfire from the list of applications, follow the instructions, and ONCE will take care of the rest.

If you prefer the command line to the dashboard, you can deploy directly:

```sh
once deploy ghcr.io/basecamp/once-campfire --host chat.example.com
```

### Deploying with Docker

If you'd rather run the Docker image yourself, you can read more about that in the [self-hosting guide](docs/self-hosting.md).

> [!TIP]
> When you start Campfire for the first time, you'll be guided through a wizard to create an admin account.
> The email address that you enter for the admin account will be visible on the sign-in page, it's there so
> that people have someone to contact if they need help with their account. If that bothers you, put in any
> email address you want and create yourself a new admin account.

## Development

You are welcome - and encouraged - to modify Campfire to your liking.
Please see our [development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Campfire set up for local development.

## Security

See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for how to report a vulnerability and a description of our trust model.

# The bot message API. A bot posts by sending the message text as the raw request body, e.g.
#
#   curl -d "Deploy of v1.2.3 finished ✅" https://chat.example.com/rooms/<room-id>/<bot-key>/messages
#
# There is no session here: the bot key in the path is the credential.
class Bots::MessagesController < ApplicationController
  allow_unauthenticated_access
  skip_forgery_protection

  before_action :set_bot, :set_room

  rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
    head :not_found
  end

  def create
    text = message_text
    return head :unprocessable_content unless text

    @message = @bot.post_text(@room, text)

    head :created, location: message_path(@message)
  end

  # Clients send curl's default form encoding, and Rails would try to parse the body as form fields before the
  # action runs, rejecting text such as "100% done". The body is the message, so it's never read as fields.
  def process_action(...)
    request.request_parameters = {}
    super
  end

  private
    def set_bot
      @bot = Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: params[:bot_key])

      unless @bot
        response.headers["WWW-Authenticate"] = %(Bot realm="Campfire")
        head :unauthorized
      end
    end

class Room::MessagePusher
  attr_reader :room, :message

  def initialize(room:, message:)
    @room, @message = room, message
  end

  def push
    build_payload.tap do |payload|
      push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
    end
  end

  private
    def build_payload
      if room.direct?
        build_direct_payload
      else
        build_shared_payload
      end
    end

    def build_direct_payload
      {
        title: message.creator.name,
        body: message.plain_text_body,
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def build_shared_payload
      {
        title: room.name,
        body: "#{message.creator.name}: #{message.plain_text_body}",
        path: Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.room_path(room)
      }
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_everything(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
    end

    def push_to_users_involved_in_mentions(payload)
      enqueue_payload_for_delivery payload, push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(message.mentionees)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_users_involved_in_everything
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_everything)
    end

    def push_subscriptions_for_mentionable_users(mentionees)
      relevant_subscriptions.merge(Membership.involved_in_mentions).where(user_id: mentionees.ids)
    end

    def relevant_subscriptions
      Push::Subscription
        .joins(user: :memberships)
        .merge(Membership.visible.disconnected.where(room: room).where.not(user: message.creator))
    end

    def enqueue_payload_for_delivery(payload, subscriptions)
      Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.queue(payload, subscriptions)
    end
end

steps.message:
`insert_all` with no rows returns an empty result, and nothing overrides Turbo's confirm, so the native `confirm()` is already in use. I now have the full picture and can lay out the design:

- **Data:** a `bots.join_all_open_rooms` boolean (default false, not null), which is the switch.
- **Bots don't auto-join:** `User`'s open-room grant skips bot users. Open-room grants (new or converted room) include only people plus bots whose switch is on.
- **Switch on:** joins every existing open room (`after_save`, inside the bot's transaction).
- **`joined` events:** `Room::Memberships#grant_to` uses `insert_all(..., returning:)` to learn exactly which memberships were inserted. For bots with a webhook in non-direct rooms, it enqueues `Bot::WebhookJob` after the transaction commits.
- **Webhook:** `Bot::Webhook` accepts either a `Message` (mention) or a `Room` (joined), and its delivery and reply logic is shared.

class Room < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :memberships, dependent: :delete_all do
    def grant_to(users)
      room = proxy_association.owner
      attributes = Array(users).collect { |user| { room_id: room.id, user_id: user.id, involvement: room.default_involvement } }

      # RETURNING only includes the memberships this grant created, so people who were already members aren't announced again.
      inserted = Membership.insert_all(attributes, returning: %i[ user_id ])
      room.announce_joined_bots(inserted.rows.flatten)
    end

    def revoke_from(users)
      destroy_by user: users
    end

    def revise(granted: [], revoked: [])
      transaction do
        grant_to(granted) if granted.present?
        revoke_from(revoked) if revoked.present?
      end
    end
  end

  has_many :messages, dependent: :destroy

  scope :closeds,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Closed") }
  scope :directs,         -> { where(type: "Rooms::Direct") }
  scope :without_directs, -> { where.not(type: "Rooms::Direct") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order("LOWER(name)") }

  class << self
    def create_for(attributes, users:)
      transaction do
        create!(attributes).tap do |room|
          room.memberships.grant_to users
        end
      end
    end

    def original
      order(:created_at).first
    end
  end

  def receive(message)
    unread_memberships(message)
    push_later(message)
    ask_mentioned_bots_later(message)
  end

  # Sends a joined event to the webhooks of the bots that were just added to this room. Direct rooms never send one.
  # The events go out once the memberships have committed, so a webhook never hears about a membership that rolls back.
  def announce_joined_bots(user_ids)
    return if direct? || user_ids.empty?

    Room.current_transaction.after_commit do
      Bot.active.with_webhook.where(user_id: user_ids).find_each do |bot|
        Bot::WebhookJob.perform_later(bot, self)
      end
    end
  end

  def open?
    is_a?(Rooms::Open)
  end

  def closed?
    is_a?(Rooms::Closed)
  end

  def direct?
    is_a?(Rooms::Direct)
  end

  def default_involvement
    "mentions"
  end

  private
    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other freely. A direct room can't become
    # either: its participants agreed to a private conversation, not to one whose
    # audience someone else gets to widen afterwards.
    def direct_rooms_keep_their_type
      if type_changed? && type_was == "Rooms::Direct"
        errors.add :type, "can't be changed for a direct room"
      end
    end

    def unread_memberships(message)
      memberships.visible.disconnected.where.not(user: message.creator).update_all(unread_at: message.created_at, updated_at: Time.current)
    end

    def push_later(message)
      Room::PushMessageJob.perform_later(self, message)
    end

    def ask_mentioned_bots_later(message)
      Room::AskMentionedBotsJob.perform_later(message)
    end
end

require "net/http"
require "zlib"
require "restricted_http/private_network_guard"

# Tells a bot's webhook about something that happened to it, and posts the bot's answer into the room when it gives one.
# Two things are told: a mention of the bot, given as the Message that mentions it, and the bot joining a room, given as
# the Room. Both are sent as a JSON POST, and both are answered the same way:
#
# - 200 with a text/plain or text/html body: the body is posted into the room as the bot's message.
# - 204, or any other response: nothing is posted. Redirects aren't followed.
#
# Webhook URLs are set by members, so they're fetched the way link unfurling fetches URLs: addresses that are private
# or internal are refused, and the checked address is the one connected to, so a DNS change can't redirect the request.
#
# This runs in a job, so the person who posted the message never waits on the bot.
class Bot::Webhook
  OPEN_TIMEOUT = 5 # seconds to connect
  READ_TIMEOUT = 15 # seconds between reads
  DEADLINE = 30 # seconds for the whole exchange, so a bot can't drip out its answer and hold a worker

  MAX_REPLY_SIZE = 64.kilobytes
  REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES = %w[ text/plain text/html ]

  # Ways a webhook can fail that aren't a bug here: refused addresses, unreachable or misbehaving servers, and
  # responses that can't be read. Anything else is left to raise, so it reaches the job's error reporting.
  FAILURES = [
    RestrictedHTTP::Violation, Surfguard::Unresolvable, URI::InvalidURIError, Timeout::Error,
    SocketError, SystemCallError, IOError, OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError, Net::ProtocolError, Net::HTTPBadResponse,
    Net::HTTPHeaderSyntaxError, Zlib::Error
  ]

  # Content from a bot is sanitized the same way as the room's messages. The same filters run when a message is
  # displayed, so storing clean content doesn't change what people see.
  SANITIZE = ActionText::Content::Filters.new(ContentFilters::SanitizeTags, ContentFilters::SanitizeAttributes)

  attr_reader :bot, :message, :room

  # The subject is a Message that mentions the bot, or a Room that the bot has just joined.
  def initialize(bot, subject)
    @bot = bot
    @message = subject if subject.is_a?(Message)
    @room = subject.is_a?(Room) ? subject : subject.room
  end

  def deliver
    return unless bot.user.active? && bot.webhook_url && member_of_room?

    reply = fetch_reply
    post_reply(*reply) if reply
  rescue *FAILURES => e
    Rails.logger.warn "Webhook for bot #{bot.id} failed without a reply: #{e.class}"
  end

  # The JSON sent to the webhook. Paths are relative: the bot knows its Campfire origin.
  def payload
    message ? mention_payload : joined_payload
  end

  private
    def mention_payload
      {
        event: "mention",
        author: { id: message.creator.id, name: message.creator.name },
        room: room_json,
        message: {
          id: message.id,
          body: { text: text, html: html },
          link: routes.room_at_message_path(room, message)
        }
      }
    end

    def joined_payload
      { event: "joined", room: room_json }
    end

    def room_json
      { id: room.id, name: room_name, reply_to: routes.room_bot_messages_path(room, bot.bot_key) }
    end

    def routes
      Rails.application.routes.url_helpers
    end

    # The bot may have been removed from the room after the message was posted.
    def member_of_room?
      room.users.exists?(bot.user_id)
    end

    def uri
      @uri ||= URI.parse(bot.webhook_url)
    end

    def room_name
      if room.direct?
        room.users.where.not(id: bot.user_id).pluck(:name).to_sentence.presence || bot.name
      else
        room.name
      end
    end

    # The message as text, with this bot's own @mention taken out, so that it reads as the command addressed to the bot.
    def text
      @text ||= content_without_bot_mention.to_plain_text.gsub(/[ \t]{2,}/, " ").strip
    end

    def content_without_bot_mention
      fragment = message.body.body.fragment.replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) do |node|
        ActionText::Attachable.from_node(node) == bot.user ? nil : node
      end

      ActionText::Content.new(fragment, canonicalize: false)
    end

    # The whole message as rich text, mentions included.
    def html
      @html ||= SANITIZE.apply(message.body.body).to_html
    end

    # Returns [content type, text] for an answer that should be posted, or nil.
    def fetch_reply
      Timeout.timeout(DEADLINE) do
        address = RestrictedHTTP::PrivateNetworkGuard.resolve(uri.hostname)

        Net::HTTP.start(uri.hostname, uri.port, ipaddr: address, use_ssl: uri.scheme == "https",
            open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT) do |http|
          http.request(post_request) do |response|
            # Returning from inside the block leaves the response unread, so a large or endless body isn't downloaded.
            return reply_from(response)
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def post_request
      Net::HTTP::Post.new(uri.request_uri, "Content-Type" => "application/json").tap do |request|
        request.body = payload.to_json
      end
    end

    def reply_from(response)
      content_type = response.content_type.to_s.downcase

      return unless response.is_a?(Net::HTTPOK) && REPLY_CONTENT_TYPES.include?(content_type)

      if body = read_capped_body(response)
        [ content_type, decode(body, response.type_params["charset"]) ]
      end
    end

    # Nil if the body is larger than a reply can be.
    def read_capped_body(response)
      body = String.new

      response.read_body do |chunk|
        body << chunk
        return if body.bytesize > MAX_REPLY_SIZE
      end

      body
    end

    # The body as UTF-8 text, or nil when it isn't valid in its charset. A reply that doesn't name one is UTF-8.
    def decode(body, charset)
      text = body.force_encoding(charset || Encoding::UTF_8).encode(Encoding::UTF_8)
      text if text.valid_encoding?
    rescue EncodingError, ArgumentError
      nil
    end

    def post_reply(content_type, text)
      return if text.nil?

      # The bot may have left the room while its webhook was answering.
      return unless member_of_room?

      if content_type == "text/html"
        post_html_reply(text)
      else
        post_text_reply(text)
      end
    end

    def post_text_reply(text)
      text = text.strip
      bot.post_text(room, text) if text.present?
    end

    def post_html_reply(html)
      content = sanitized_reply(html)
      bot.post_html(room, content.to_html) if content.to_plain_text.present?
    end

    # A bot's HTML is posted without attachments. A mention or other attachment would notify people, and trigger
    # bots, as though a person had written it.
    def sanitized_reply(html)
      fragment = ActionText::Fragment.from_html(html).replace(ActionText::Attachment.tag_name) { nil }

      SANITIZE.apply(ActionText::Content.new(fragment, canonicalize: false))
    end
end
EOF
cat > app/jobs/bot/webhook_job.rb <<'EOF'
class Bot::WebhookJob < ApplicationJob
  # The bot, or the message or room it's asked about, may be deleted before the job runs. Then there's nothing to ask.
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  # The subject is a Message that mentions the bot, or a Room that the bot has joined.
  def perform(bot, subject)
    Bot::Webhook.new(bot, subject).deliver
  end
end
EOF

cd /app && cat > test/models/bot_test.rb <<'EOF'
require "test_helper"

class BotTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  setup do
    @creator = users(:david)
  end

  test "creating a bot creates a user with its name, which is a bot" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", bot.name
    assert_equal "Deploy Bot", bot.user.name
    assert bot.user.bot?
    assert_equal bot, bot.user.bot
  end

  test "creating a bot defaults the creator to the current user" do
    Current.set(user: @creator) do
      assert_equal @creator, Bot.create!(name: "Current Bot").creator
    end
  end

  test "a new bot joins no open rooms unless it's set to join all of them" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    assert_not bot.join_all_open_rooms?
    assert_empty bot.user.rooms
  end

  test "a bot set to join all open rooms is a member of every open room, but not of closed rooms" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.user.rooms.opens.count
    assert_not_includes bot.user.rooms, rooms(:watercooler)
  end

  test "turning the switch on adds the bot to the open rooms that exist" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    bot.update!(join_all_open_rooms: true)

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.user.rooms.opens.count
    assert_not_includes bot.user.rooms, rooms(:watercooler)
  end

  test "turning the switch off keeps the bot's current memberships" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)

    bot.update!(join_all_open_rooms: false)

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, bot.user.rooms.opens.count
  end

  test "turning the switch off stops the bot joining open rooms created later" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)
    bot.update!(join_all_open_rooms: false)

    room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Later", creator: @creator)

    assert_not_includes room.users, bot.user
  end

  test "an open room created later adds the bots that join all open rooms, and no others" do
    joining = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)
    quiet = Bot.create!(name: "Quiet Bot", creator: @creator)

    room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Later", creator: @creator)

    assert_includes room.users, joining.user
    assert_not_includes room.users, quiet.user
  end

  test "a closed room that becomes open adds the bots that join all open rooms" do
    joining = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)

    room = rooms(:watercooler).becomes!(Rooms::Open)
    room.save!

    assert_includes room.users, joining.user
  end

  test "a bot's switch being on for a bot that's saved again doesn't add it to rooms again" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)
    room = Rooms::Open.create!(name: "Later", creator: @creator)
    assert_includes room.users, bot.user

    room.memberships.where(user: bot.user).delete_all
    bot.update!(name: "Renamed Bot")

    assert_not_includes room.users.reload, bot.user
  end

  test "a bot key is unique and unguessably long" do
    first = Bot.create!(name: "First", creator: @creator)
    second = Bot.create!(name: "Second", creator: @creator)

    assert_operator first.bot_key.length, :>=, 24
    assert_not_equal first.bot_key, second.bot_key
  end

  test "a bot needs a name" do
    bot = Bot.new(creator: @creator, name: "")

    assert_not bot.valid?
    assert bot.errors.of_kind?(:name, :blank)
  end

  test "renaming and changing the avatar go through the bot's user" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    bot.update!(name: "Renamed Bot", avatar: file_fixture("moon.jpg").open)

    assert_equal "Renamed Bot", bot.reload.user.name
    assert bot.user.avatar.attached?
  end

  test "a bot's user can't sign in, since nobody knows its password" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    assert_not bot.user.authenticate("secret123456")
    assert_nil User.active.authenticate_by(email_address: nil, password: "secret123456")
  end

  test "a person's user isn't a bot" do
    assert_not users(:david).bot?
  end

  test "people still join every open room when they're created, unlike bots" do
    person = User.create!(name: "New Person", password: "secret123456")

    assert_equal Rooms::Open.count, person.rooms.opens.count
  end

  test "deactivating a bot deactivates its user, removes it from rooms, and deletes its bot key" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, join_all_open_rooms: true)
    user = bot.user
    bot_key = bot.bot_key
    assert user.memberships.without_direct_rooms.any?

    bot.deactivate

    assert user.reload.deactivated?
    assert_equal 0, user.memberships.without_direct_rooms.count
    assert_not Bot.exists?(bot.id)
    assert_nil Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: bot_key)
  end

  test "only bots whose users are active can authenticate" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)
    assert_equal bot, Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: bot.bot_key)

    bot.user.update!(status: :banned)
    assert_nil Bot.active.find_by(bot_key: bot.bot_key)
  end

  test "a webhook URL is optional" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Quiet Bot", creator: @creator)

    assert_nil bot.reload.webhook_url
  end

  test "a blank webhook URL removes the webhook" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, webhook_url: "https://hooks.example.com/deploy")

    bot.update!(webhook_url: "  ")

    assert_nil bot.reload.webhook_url
    assert_not_includes Bot.with_webhook, bot
  end

  test "a webhook URL is an http or https URL" do
    [ "https://hooks.example.com/deploy", "http://ci.internal:8080/hook?token=1" ].each do |url|
      assert Bot.new(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, webhook_url: url).valid?, url
    end

    [ "hooks.example.com/deploy", "ftp://hooks.example.com/deploy", "https://", "not a url", "https://exa mple.com" ].each do |url|
      bot = Bot.new(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, webhook_url: url)

      assert_not bot.valid?, url
      assert bot.errors.of_kind?(:webhook_url, :invalid), url
    end
  end

  test "a webhook URL can carry a secret, so it's filtered from logged parameters and the bot's inspection" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator, webhook_url: "https://hooks.example.com/secret-token")
    filter = ActiveSupport::ParameterFilter.new(Rails.application.config.filter_parameters)

    assert_equal "[FILTERED]", filter.filter(bot: { webhook_url: "https://hooks.example.com/secret-token" })[:bot][:webhook_url]
    assert_not_includes bot.inspect, "secret-token"
  end

  test "the bot key is filtered out of the bot's inspected attributes" do
    bot = Bot.create!(name: "Deploy Bot", creator: @creator)

    assert_not_includes bot.inspect, bot.bot_key
  end
end
EOF

steps.message: The sign-in form has `type=email` and `type=password` inputs, and the rest of the bot form uses placeholders and labels. I'll write a Ferrum script that signs in, creates a bot through the UI with the switch on, then edits a second bot to turn the switch on and off. It will check the database after each step.

arguments.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/browser && cat > /tmp/browser/verify_bot_form.rb <<'EOF'
require "ferrum"

BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:3100"
browser = Ferrum::Browser.new(browser_path: "/usr/bin/chromium", headless: true, timeout: 30, process_timeout: 60,
  browser_options: { "no-sandbox" => nil, "disable-dev-shm-usage" => nil, "disable-gpu" => nil })

def checked?(browser)
  browser.evaluate("document.querySelector(\"input[name='bot[join_all_open_rooms]'][type=checkbox]\").checked")
end

def label_present?(browser)
  browser.evaluate("[...document.querySelectorAll('label')].some(l => l.textContent.trim() === 'Add to all open rooms')")
end

begin
  browser.goto("#{BASE}/session/new")
  browser.at_css("input[type=email]").focus.type("admin@example.com")
  browser.at_css("input[type=password]").focus.type("secret123456")
  browser.at_css("form button[type=submit]").click
  sleep 2
  puts "signed in, url=#{browser.current_url}"

  browser.goto("#{BASE}/bots/new")
  sleep 1
  puts "new form: label present=#{label_present?(browser)} checkbox checked by default=#{checked?(browser)}"

  browser.at_xpath("//label[normalize-space(.)='Add to all open rooms']").click
  puts "after clicking the label: checked=#{checked?(browser)}"

  browser.at_css("input[placeholder='Name the bot']").focus.type("Browser Bot")
  browser.at_css("input[placeholder='Webhook URL']").focus.type("https://hooks.example.com/browser-bot")
  browser.at_css("form[action='/bots'] button[type=submit]").click
  sleep 2
  puts "after saving new bot: url=#{browser.current_url}"

  browser.goto("#{BASE}/bots/new")
  sleep 1
  browser.at_css("input[placeholder='Name the bot']").focus.type("Quiet Browser Bot")
  browser.at_css("form[action='/bots'] button[type=submit]").click
  sleep 2
  puts "saved quiet bot (switch left off): url=#{browser.current_url}"

  # Edit the quiet bot and turn the switch on
  quiet_edit = browser.current_url.sub(/\/bots.*/, "") + "/bots"
  browser.goto("#{BASE}/bots")
  sleep 1
  edit_links = browser.evaluate("[...document.querySelectorAll('a')].map(a => a.getAttribute('href')).filter(h => h && h.match(/\\/bots\\/\\d+\\/edit/))")
  puts "edit links: #{edit_links.inspect}"
  quiet_link = browser.evaluate("(() => { const li = [...document.querySelectorAll('li')].find(li => li.textContent.includes('Quiet Browser Bot')); return li.querySelector('a').getAttribute('href') })()")
  browser.goto("#{BASE}#{quiet_link}")
  sleep 1
  puts "edit page for quiet bot: checked=#{checked?(browser)}"
  browser.at_xpath("//label[normalize-space(.)='Add to all open rooms']").click
  puts "edit page after turning on: checked=#{checked?(browser)}"
  browser.at_css("form button[type=submit]").click
  sleep 2
  puts "after saving edit: url=#{browser.current_url}"

  # Re-open the edit page: should show it on, then turn it off and save
  browser.goto("#{BASE}#{quiet_link}")
  sleep 1
  puts "reopened edit page: checked=#{checked?(browser)}"
  browser.at_xpath("//label[normalize-space(.)='Add to all open rooms']").click
  puts "after turning off: checked=#{checked?(browser)}"
  browser.at_css("form button[type=submit]").click
  sleep 2
  puts "after saving with switch off: url=#{browser.current_url}"
  browser.goto("#{BASE}#{quiet_link}")
  sleep 1
  puts "reopened edit page after off: checked=#{checked?(browser)}"
ensure
  browser.quit
end
EOF

inside one it waits for the commit. A rolled-back grant queues nothing, and a job never runs before the membership it
announces exists.

which skips bots). A bot gets open rooms only through its switch, a boolean column on `bots` (`join_all_open_rooms`,

Reviewing `announce_joined_bots` again, I spotted a real scaling risk. `where(user_id: user_ids)` puts every newly inserted user ID into one SQL `IN` list. When an open room is created, that's every person on the account, and SQLite caps bound variables, so very large accounts could hit a failure after commit. Bots are few, so it's cheaper to load the active webhook bots and match their user IDs against a set in Ruby. I'll make that change and re-run the room tests.

  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "## Joining rooms (webhooks)

Whenever a bot is added to a room, its webhook receives a `joined` event, once for each room it joins. That holds
whether a person added the bot (to a closed room, or with the switch on its page) or an open room picked it up when the
room was created. Direct conversations never send it, and neither does a bot without a webhook URL.

```json
{
  "event": "joined",
  "room": { "id": 5, "name": "Ops", "reply_to": "/rooms/5/<bot-code>/messages" }
}
```

- `room.id` and `room.name` are the room. `room.reply_to` is the bot's posting URL for the room, as for a mention.
- The bot answers the same way as for a mention. A `200` with `Content-Type: text/plain` or `text/html` is posted into
  the room as the bot's message, so a bot can say hello that way. A `204`, or any other response, posts nothing.
- The event is sent once the membership has committed. A membership that is rolled back sends nothing, and a bot that
  has left the room by the time its webhook answers doesn't post.
- Adding a bot back after it was removed is a new join, so it is announced again. Granting a bot a room it is already
  in announces nothing.

## Design notes
"
}

steps.message:
Bots no longer join open rooms by default, and the switch, the open-room join, and the `joined` events are in place. The full unit suite passes (454 runs, 0 failures; the 22 skips are the same DNS-dependent tests as the baseline), and RuboCop and Brakeman are clean.

## What changed

**Switch and data**
- Migration adds `bots.join_all_open_rooms` (boolean, default false, not null).
- The bot form (`bots/_form.html.erb`, shared by new and edit) has an "Add to all open rooms" switch. It's a real checkbox inside a `<label>`, styled as a switch, and off by default.
- `BotsController` permits the new field.

**Joining**
- `User` grants open-room membership to people only. Bots are skipped.
- `Rooms::Open` grants new open rooms (created or converted from closed) to `User.joining_open_rooms`: people plus bots with the switch on.
- Turning the switch on joins every existing open room, inside the bot's save transaction. Turning it off keeps memberships.

**`joined` events**
- `Room::Memberships#grant_to` now uses `insert_all(..., returning:)`, so it knows exactly which memberships were created. Already-present members are never announced twice.
- `Room#announce_joined_bots` enqueues `Bot::WebhookJob` for each newly joined bot that has a webhook. It's skipped for direct rooms and runs after commit, so a rolled-back grant sends nothing.
- `Bot::Webhook` accepts a `Message` (mention) or a `Room` (joined). Delivery and reply posting are shared, so a 200 text or HTML reply gets posted into the room.

**Docs and tests**
- `docs/bots.md` covers the switch, the `joined` payload and reply rules, the join design, and the code map. The README line is updated too.
- I replaced the outdated "joins every open room" tests and added coverage for the switch, `joined` exactly-once behavior, direct rooms, commit/rollback timing, bans, the form, and the closed-room path.

## Verification beyond unit tests
Chromedriver isn't available offline, so the repo's system tests couldn't run. Instead I drove the dev server in Chromium via Ferrum:
- The label is present, and the switch is unchecked by default. Clicking the label toggles it.
- Creating a bot with the switch on joined both open rooms. Turning the switch on for an existing bot joined it, and turning it off kept its memberships.
- The switch renders at 48×28 px with a zero-size real checkbox inside the label.
- Deleting a bot raises the native `confirm()` with the expected message.

## Decisions to review
- **Existing bots** keep their current memberships, and their switch defaults to off, so they won't pick up future open rooms. The migration doesn't backfill.
- **`reply_to` format:** the spec's example shows a different code shape (`42-Xy3abc9defGh`). I kept the bot's existing `bot_key` for consistency with mention payloads and the posting endpoint.
- **Subject-typed webhook:** `Bot::Webhook.new(bot, message)` still works for mentions, and `Bot::Webhook.new(bot, room)` handles joins. The alternative was a larger refactor.
